title: Stochastic batch tinker log - afternoon session
content:
Context:
Working on intermittent p99 spikes for generative workloads when we enable stochastic batching (variable batch sizes based on request arrival). Goal: capture quick experiments, hypotheses, repro steps, and immediate TODOs so I don't forget between switches.

Quick summary of what I saw (afternoon run, local rig: 8xA100-80GB, runtime@b2f3c4d):
- Baseline (deterministic batch=8): throughput ~850 toks/s, p50 18ms, p95 60ms, p99 110ms.
- Stochastic batching (target mean=8, CV~0.45): throughput ~880 toks/s, p50 16ms, p95 75ms, p99 260-320ms (spiky).
- Spikes correlate with ~15% of requests that end up as singleton batches during brief bursts in arrival pattern.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV-cache eviction/rehash path under variable batch sizes causes lock contention (shared structure guarded by single mutex). When many small batches happen, we do more frequent KV ops -> contention -> tail latency.
2) Kernel launch overhead: small batches cause many more kernel launches that hit a non-amortized scheduling path (especially for fused-attn kernels with small sequence lengths).
3) Batching scheduler thrashes between pack/unpack codepaths when batchsize oscillates, leaving CPU scheduling jitter that cascades to GPU queuing.
4) Metric/reporting artifact: our p99 calculation window is per-second, but the queueing jitter causes transient spikes that inflate p99 — still real user-visible, but maybe shorter-lived than it looks.

Quick experiments run (commands + notes):
- Repro script: python -m rwserve.bench --model redwood-13b --arrival-pattern poisson --mean-rps 60 --target-bucket-mean 8 --stochastic --rng-seed 42
- Baseline run pinned to runtime@b2f3c4d: reproduced p99 ~115ms.
- Stochastic run with deterministic KV-fastpath disabled (env KV_FASTPATH=0): p99 fell to ~140ms (still higher than baseline but better than 260ms).
- Stochastic run with batch-capping (max_batch=16): p99 ~180ms.
Notes: KV_FASTPATH toggle reduced the worst tails; points to hotpath there.

Observations from flamegraphs (CPU side, perf on on-host):
- Long pause in thread 'batching-0' where it holds kv_map mutex for ~12-20ms occasionally.
- 'rpc-handler' threads pile up behind that lock; GPU queue shows bursts of submissions.
- nvprof traces show many small kernel launches clustered instead of amortized big kernels.

Immediate small fixes to try (short, can test today):
- [ ] Add per-worker KV maps (shard by worker id) to reduce global lock contention (fast to prototype).
- [ ] Implement heuristic: prefer grouping requests up to a min effective batch size (min_effective=4) before releasing to GPU (reduces singletons).
- [ ] Add jitter smoothing: if arrival rate oscillates, add small buffering window (20ms) before flush.
- [ ] Instrument counters: count singleton-batch fraction per-second and expose in /metrics.

Repro steps for devs (minimal):
1) git checkout b2f3c4d && make bench-image
2) docker run -e KV_FASTPATH=1 -p 8080:8080 runtime-bench:local 
3) python tools/load_gen.py --target http://localhost:8080/generate --pattern poisson --rps 60 --duration 120 --seed 42
4) collect metrics via prometheus endpoint /metrics and trace /tracing

Longer-term thoughts (not for today):
- Rework KV map to be sharded with lock-free read paths (sounds like 2–3 wks of focused work + tests).
- Consider backpressure: if batch execution latency rises, throttle acceptance for small requests (dangerous for PLG UX).
- Model-aware batching: certain models with short seqs benefit from merging more aggressively; route those requests to a different pool with tuned batch strategy.

Linked/informative threads:
- RW-2121 (eviction thundering) has related history; assign notes overlap.
- PR #987 adds basic singleton metrics; use it to capture fraction of singleton batches in the next run.

Notes for pairing with Rohan tomorrow (agenda):
- Walk through the perf flamegraph and point to kv_map mutex hotspots.
- Test per-worker KV shard prototype (I will push a branch early AM).
- Decide on quick rollout: enable min_effective batch heuristic behind runtime flag and run A/B on canary pool.

Open questions / unknowns to answer in follow-up:
- Is the mutex actually in userland code or in a third-party library (tests above suggest ours, but need confirm).
- How does this behavior change under Dedicated (reserved capacity) vs hosted noisy neighbors? replicate on dedicated staging.
- Any downstream feature (console tracing hooks) that would make this easier for customer debugging?

Todo (concrete):
- [ ] Push prototype: per-worker-kv branch (mei/protobuf-kv-shard) — target EOD tomorrow.
- [ ] Add singleton-batch exporter via PR #987 (wire to prometheus).
- [ ] Run stochastic workload with KV_FASTPATH=0 on dedicated-staging (request infra slot from SRE).
- [ ] Draft short blurb for triage channel: "stochastic-batching p99 spikes: hypothesis kv contention" with attachments (flamegraph, nvprof).

Random micro-notes/to-self:
- Check kernel build flags: compiled with -O2 but not LTO; might be able to squeeze launch overhead with link-time opts.
- Look at nvlink utilization during spikes — might reveal inter-GPU stalls.
- Remember to tag PRs with RW-2121.

Meeting snippet (15:45 quick sync with Ivy):
- Ivy: "If we shard KV by worker, we need to ensure cache warm-up per-shard isn't expensive."
- Me: "Plan: lazy warm-up + shared prefetch during low-load periods."
- Action: Ivy will sketch warm-up heuristic by EOD.

End note: keep the next run reproducible; save the load_gen seed and attach all logs. If this goes to canary, include singleton fraction histogram in the release notes so SRE can roll back quickly.

-- Mei
